_README.purpose: What to use INSTEAD of an ingredient someone reacts to.
_README.why_not_embeddings: The original plan was FAISS over FoodBERT/Food2Vec embeddings. That is the wrong objective: embeddings encode which ingredients are SIMILAR, and cream is extremely similar to milk because they co-occur constantly in recipes. A substitution engine that suggests cream for milk is worse than useless to someone with a dairy allergy. Substitution needs functional equivalence PLUS allergen difference, which similarity alone cannot express. So this is curated.
_README.safety_rule: Every suggestion is re-checked against the user's own profile before display. A substitute that is dairy-free but contains tree nuts must never be offered to someone with a nut allergy. `contains` exists for exactly that check.
_README.context: baking = structure and chemistry matter (fat, protein, leavening). cooking = flavour and body matter. raw = eaten as-is.
_README.STATUS: SEED DATA - kitchen-tested common knowledge, not clinically reviewed. Ratios are starting points, not guarantees.

milk.name: Oat milk
milk.notes: Closest to dairy milk in body and sweetness. Swap 1:1. The usual first choice for tea and baking.

milk.name: Soy milk
milk.notes: Highest protein of the alternatives, so it browns and sets most like dairy. Swap 1:1.

milk.name: Lactose-free milk
milk.notes: Real dairy with the lactose already broken down. Behaves identically in cooking. Fine for lactose intolerance, NOT for a milk allergy - the protein is still there.
milk._contains_note: Listed as casein, not milk, on purpose. The lactose is gone, so this must NOT flag for lactose intolerance; the milk protein remains, so it MUST flag for a dairy allergy. Listing 'milk' would have got both wrong.

milk.name: Coconut milk
milk.notes: Rich and works well in curries and sauces. Carries a distinct flavour, so not neutral.

butter.name: Olive oil
butter.notes: Use about 3/4 the volume of butter. Good for frying and sauces, wrong for pastry.

butter.name: Dairy-free block margarine
butter.notes: Swap 1:1. Use a block rather than a soft spread for baking - spreads hold too much water.

butter.name: Coconut oil
butter.notes: Solid at room temperature, so it creams like butter. Swap 1:1. Refined has less coconut flavour.

cream.name: Coconut cream
cream.notes: Whips and enriches like double cream. Chill the tin first. Adds coconut flavour.

cream.name: Oat cream
cream.notes: Neutral, pours and reduces like single cream. Will not whip.

cheese.name: Nutritional yeast
cheese.notes: Savoury and cheese-like for sauces and pasta. Not a melting cheese.

cheese.name: Plant-based hard cheese
cheese.notes: Check the base - most are cashew or coconut, which matters if nuts are also a problem.

wheat.name: Gluten-free flour blend
wheat.notes: Swap 1:1 for blends containing xanthan gum. Without it, baked goods crumble.

wheat.name: Rice flour
wheat.notes: Good for thickening and coating. Too gritty alone for bread.

wheat.name: Cornflour
wheat.notes: Thickens sauces. Use half the quantity of wheat flour.

egg.name: Flax egg
egg.notes: 1 tbsp ground flaxseed + 3 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes, per egg. Binds well; will not aerate.

egg.name: Aquafaba
egg.notes: 3 tbsp chickpea tin liquid per egg. The one substitute that actually whips to peaks.

egg.name: Mashed banana
egg.notes: Half a banana per egg in cakes and muffins. Adds sweetness and flavour.

peanuts.name: Sunflower seed butter
peanuts.notes: Closest texture and fat content to peanut butter, and seed-based rather than nut.

peanuts.name: Pumpkin seeds
peanuts.notes: For crunch in salads and stir-fries.

tree nuts.name: Toasted seeds
tree nuts.notes: Pumpkin or sunflower seeds give the crunch without nuts.

tree nuts.name: Toasted oats
tree nuts.notes: For texture in crumbles and granola.

soy.name: Coconut aminos
soy.notes: Replaces soy sauce. Sweeter and less salty, so season afterwards.

_reflux_note: The entries below are for people who have identified these as their own triggers. Pona does not assume anyone with reflux reacts to them.

tomato.name: Roasted red pepper
tomato.notes: Blended, it gives a sweet red sauce base with far less acid.

tomato.name: Pumpkin or carrot base
tomato.notes: Makes a mild, naturally sweet sauce. Works well for pasta and stews.

coffee.name: Rooibos
coffee.notes: Naturally caffeine-free, low acid, and has some of the roasted depth.

coffee.name: Chicory root drink
coffee.notes: Roasted and bitter like coffee, with no caffeine.

chocolate.name: Carob
chocolate.notes: Naturally sweet, caffeine-free and lower acid. Swap 1:1 for cocoa powder.

onion.name: Green tops of spring onion
onion.notes: The green part is much better tolerated than the bulb by many people.

onion.name: Fennel
onion.notes: Gives sweetness and aromatic base when softened slowly.
